venue.name: Nanaimo Museum
venue.description: The Nanaimo Museum is a community museum in the Vancouver Island Conference Centre in downtown Nanaimo, with permanent exhibits on Snuneymuxw culture and the city's coal mining history. Admission is by donation for everyone. It runs a published menu of guided school programs for kindergarten to grade 12, virtual programs delivered to the classroom, and self guided visits with discovery sheets. The museum also looks after the Bastion on the waterfront and an 1890s miner's cottage in Piper's Park, both of which feature in its programs.
venue.address: 100 Museum Way, Nanaimo, BC, Canada, V9R 5J8

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The museum is wheelchair accessible. Unfortunately the Bastion is not wheelchair accessible.

venue.nearby_park: Piper's Park, about a five minute walk from the museum, where the historical miner's cottage stands
restrictions: The Lantern Tour takes 90 minutes and is not suitable for anyone under the age of 12
venue.hours_notes: Fall, winter and spring: 10:00am to 4:00pm Tuesday to Saturday, from September 8, 2026 to June 26, 2027, closed Sundays, Mondays and stat holidays. Summer: 10:00am to 4:00pm Tuesday to Sunday. Hours are occasionally subject to change on short notice.
venue.seasonal_notes: School field trips are available Tuesday to Friday, September 22 to December 17, 2026 and January 19 to June 24, 2027. December is reserved for Yesteryear Christmas and Winter Lights only. The Bastion is open Saturdays, Sundays and stat holidays from July 4 to September 7, 2026, and by appointment the rest of the year.

programs.name: Snuneymuxw Seasons
programs.description: A 90 minute guided program at the museum for kindergarten to grade 2. Children learn about seasonal migration patterns and see how tools were made and used to create homes, art and prepare food. Each child receives their own mini loom for the weaving part. The price is $75 per class. Sessions run Tuesday to Friday, morning or afternoon.
programs.what_children_do: Take part in hands on activities with a museum educator, look at how tools were made and used for homes, art and food, and weave on a small loom of their own.
programs.our_note: The fee is for the whole class, not for each child, so a full class is the cheapest way to do it. Sessions only run Tuesday to Friday, so a Monday outing is not an option.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible and the session is entirely indoors. Washrooms, somewhere to eat lunch and how many adults you need are not on the site, so it is worth a call before you book.

programs.name: Petroglyphs
programs.description: A 90 minute guided program at the museum for kindergarten to grade 2 about Snuneymuxw rock art, including making petroglyph rubbings. The price is $75 per class. Sessions run Tuesday to Friday, morning or afternoon. The dates shown on this program's own page belong to the previous school year.
programs.what_children_do: Make petroglyph rubbings and find out about the animal, human and supernatural being symbols carved in Snuneymuxw territory.
programs.our_note: The dates on this one's own page are a school year out of date, so check it is still running before you build a term around it. Everything else the museum publishes says field trips run Tuesday to Friday from late September.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible and the session is entirely indoors. Washrooms, somewhere to eat lunch and how many adults you need are not on the site, so it is worth a call before you book.

programs.name: Coal Miner's Child
programs.description: A 90 minute guided program at the museum for grades 1 and 2 about children's lives in coal mining families a hundred years ago. It includes a walk outdoors to the historical miner's cottage in Piper's Park, about five minutes from the museum. The price is $75 per class. Sessions run Tuesday to Friday, morning or afternoon.
programs.what_children_do: Sit at a wooden desk with an ink well for a lesson from a strict teacher, play with toys that were popular in the early 1900s, then walk to the miner's cottage and look through it.
programs.our_note: Part of this one is outdoors and on foot, so dress the group for the weather. The museum asks you to send accessibility questions to Steph rather than answering them on the page, so raise anything about the walk when you enquire.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible but this program includes a five minute walk outdoors to the cottage. Washrooms, somewhere to eat lunch and how many adults you need are not on the site, so it is worth a call before you book.

programs.name: Bastion Tour add on module
programs.description: A 30 minute guided tour of the Bastion, Nanaimo's oldest building, added on to another museum program. Three floors of exhibits about the Hudson's Bay Company in Nanaimo, for kindergarten to grade 12. The price is $25 per class and the 30 minutes includes the walk from the museum. Available September to October and March to June, Tuesday to Friday. To book it you add Bastion tour in the comments on the museum's enquiry form.
programs.what_children_do: Walk from the museum down to the Bastion and go up through its three floors of exhibits with a guide.
programs.our_note: The Bastion is not wheelchair accessible, and the half hour counts the walk there, so the time actually inside is short. It is an add on rather than a visit on its own, so pair it with one of the longer programs.
programs.practical_summary: The Bastion is not wheelchair accessible and this one involves a walk outdoors in each direction. Washrooms, somewhere to eat lunch and how many adults you need are not on the site, so it is worth a call before you book.
programs.evidence: 30 minute guided Bastion tour add-on module $25 (Grades K-12)

programs.name: Self Guided Discovery Program
programs.description: Bring your own group through the galleries using discovery sheets that ask children to match pictures with objects on display. Each exhibit area has its own sheet and a customisable set of four sheets makes up one clipboard, which costs $0.75. Museum admission is by donation and chaperones are complimentary. You have to register in advance.
programs.what_children_do: Move through the exhibit areas at their own pace with a clipboard, matching the pictures on the sheets to objects in the gallery and answering the questions.
programs.our_note: This is the cheapest way to bring a group in and you set the pace, which suits younger children better than a timed tour. It still has to be arranged ahead, so do not treat it as a drop in.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible and the whole visit is indoors. Washrooms, somewhere to eat lunch and how many adults you need are not on the site, so it is worth a call before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: Discovery sheets are $0.75 per clipboard and a clipboard is a set of four sheets. Museum admission is by donation, and chaperones are complimentary.
programs.evidence: Discovery Sheets $0.75/clipboard plus Regular Admission per student (chaperones complimentary)

programs.name: Virtual Yesteryear Christmas
programs.description: A pre recorded virtual tour of the miner's cottage before and after it is decorated for Christmas, made for kindergarten to grade 3. About 20 minutes, $30 per class. Pre recorded programs come with one month of access, so you can break the material up or replay it. A live question and answer session with a museum educator can be added on.
programs.what_children_do: Watch from the classroom as the camera moves through the miner's cottage, looking at a candle lit tree, homemade ornaments and wooden toys.
programs.our_note: This is a video rather than a live session, so it works on a morning with no bus and no budget for one. If you want children talking back to someone, the live follow up question and answer is priced separately at $10 a class.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing has to be arranged at your end beyond a screen, since the museum sends the material to you. Whether it runs outside December is not stated, so ask when you enquire.
programs.extra_fees_note: The live follow up question and answer session is a separate virtual add on at $10 per class for 15 to 20 minutes, delivered over Teams or Zoom.

programs.name: Private Gallery Tour
programs.description: A 45 minute guided tour of the museum's exhibits, bookable by any group and available year round. A flat $65 covers up to 10 guests, then each additional guest is $6.50, up to a maximum of 25 people. All tours must be booked in advance. No age range is published for it.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the galleries with one of the museum's guides, who talks them through the exhibits on the way.
programs.our_note: No age range is attached to this one, so it is the thing to ask about if your group is younger than the school programs reach. Forty five minutes on their feet in the galleries is a long stretch for under fives, so ask whether they can sit down partway.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible and the tour is indoors. Washrooms, somewhere to eat lunch and how many adults you need are not on the site, so it is worth a call before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $65 covers up to 10 guests. Each additional guest costs $6.50, up to a tour maximum of 25 people.
programs.evidence: The cost is a flat rate of $65 for up to 10 guests.

images.alt: A guide talks to a group of about a dozen adults standing on a paved plaza outside a lit building entrance at dusk.
Children sit cross legged on the floor of a room with their arms raised over their heads, facing an adult standing at the front.
A line of children walks across a lawn towards a small white cottage with a shingled roof, where an adult in a long dress stands in the doorway.
Visitors stand on a polished concrete floor in a bright gallery, looking at large framed paintings hung along a white wall.

gaps: Youngest age for a group: not answered for under fives. The school programs are published in grades from kindergarten up, and the home learner page says the in person field trips suit learners aged 5 to 18. Nothing on the site addresses preschool or daycare groups, so ask directly whether a group of three and four year olds can book.
How many adults have to come: no ratio is published anywhere on the site for school or group visits.

Group size: no maximum or minimum is published for the school programs. The booking form asks how many participants and how many classes, and offers 1, 2 or 3 classes. The only numbers on the site are for private tours, which cap at 25, and for home learner groups, which need at least 8 learners to book a private session.

Lead time: not published as a number. The private tours page says all tours must be booked in advance and the self guided program says pre registration is required. The school programs page warns that replies from Steph can take a week or more, which is the closest thing to a lead time on the site.
Washrooms: not stated anywhere on the site.
Somewhere to eat lunch: not stated. The museum sits inside the Vancouver Island Conference Centre in the downtown core, but nothing on the site offers a room or a spot for a group to eat.
Bus parking: not stated. The location page points at a downtown parking link run by the business association rather than saying anything about coaches.
Stroller access: not stated, though the museum says it is wheelchair accessible.
Booking email: the museum's address is hidden behind Cloudflare email protection on every page, so it cannot be read. Use the enquiry form on the school programs page or the phone number.
Admission: the site says admission is by donation for everyone rather than giving a child or adult price, so there is no figure to record.

Prices are for the 2026-2027 school year. The school programs page is headed for that year and the individual program pages carry $75 per class, $25 per class for a 30 minute module, $30 per class for a pre recorded virtual program and $10 per class for a live virtual add on.
Whether the virtual Yesteryear Christmas program runs outside December is not stated on its page, so its months are unknown.
Months for Petroglyphs are unknown because its own page still shows the previous school year's dates.

Not every published program is recorded here. The site also lists Yesteryear Christmas (K-2), Winter Lights (K-3), Snuneymuxw Traditional Life (grade 3), Black Diamonds (grade 5), North West Coast First Nations Art (grades 5-7), an ESL tour for all ages, and three more virtual programs. We recorded the ones whose own pages we read, so ask for the full menu and confirm the price of any of the others.

A limited time add on for the Hope Meets Action feature exhibit runs October 2026 to February 2027 at $25 per class for 30 minutes, but the museum says it is best suited to middle and high school students, so it is not recorded as a program here.

In person modules at $25 per class for 30 minutes can be added to any program or combined into a custom one. The topics are the feature exhibit, the Bastion, the story of Snuneymuxw, Snuneymuxw tools, Snuneymuxw weaving, the coal mine, the century classroom and old fashioned toys.
Classroom and resource kits are listed on the site as unavailable at this time.
The main photo the site offers for sharing is a plain social card rather than a photograph, so the header image here is the entrance photograph from their tours page instead.

Photographs on this site are mostly loaded as page backgrounds rather than as ordinary images, so they were collected from the live page. Each one was opened and looked at before its description was written.

The site was carrying two different notices while we read it, one saying email was down and to phone, another saying the phone lines were patchy and to email. Both are likely temporary, but if one route goes quiet, try the other.

conflicts.note: Their main school pages give this year's field trip dates, but the Petroglyphs page still shows last year's, which have already finished. Take the newer dates and confirm Petroglyphs is still on the menu when you enquire.

Two sets of opening hours are floating around their site. The table on the page says Tuesday to Saturday, 10 to 4, while an older line still says Monday to Saturday, 10 to 5, and that older one is what shows up in search results. Go with Tuesday to Saturday, 10 to 4, and check the banner at the top of their home page on the day.

Their pages give two different age ranges for the Bastion tour. The card on the school programs list says kindergarten to grade 7, while the tour's own page and their booking form both say kindergarten to grade 12. Either way it takes in the youngest grades, so it only matters if you are booking older students.
